screenshots.title: Locate the source and design grid
screenshots.instruction: The source card lists available fields. The grid below it describes the query: Field, Table, Sort, Show and Criteria. The top selector strip selects whole columns; the Field row edits their contents.

screenshots.title: Apply the current design
screenshots.instruction: Scroll below the query editor and click Apply query. The status reports 32 of 32 synthetic source rows and 32 result rows. Editing the design leaves the previous result visible until you apply again.

screenshots.title: Click a source field
screenshots.instruction: Click qty in the S071_Rows source card. Desktop users can also drag a source field onto a grid column to insert before it.

screenshots.title: Find the new occurrence
screenshots.instruction: A second Qty column appears at the right. It has its own Show, Sort and Criteria controls. Scroll horizontally if needed.

screenshots.title: Choose a source, then set an alias
screenshots.instruction: In the new column’s Field dropdown choose UnitPrice. In the text box below it, press Enter/F2, type PriceCopy: [price], then Enter. The alias changes the output heading; the source remains price.

screenshots.title: Select one column
screenshots.instruction: Click the ▾ selector above Qty in the top Column row. The column receives a visible selection border and its selector becomes pressed. Its accessible name identifies the column.

screenshots.title: Select a continuous range
screenshots.instruction: Hold Shift and click the ▾ selector above Enabled. Qty, UnitPrice and Enabled are now selected. Keyboard alternative: focus a cell, Ctrl+Space, then Shift+Left/Right.

screenshots.title: Select separate columns
screenshots.instruction: Press Escape to clear the range. Click Region’s ▾ selector, then hold Ctrl (Cmd on macOS) and click UnitPrice’s ▾ selector. Two separated columns are selected.

screenshots.title: Deselect all columns
screenshots.instruction: Click Cancel selection or press Escape. Selected 0 confirms that no columns are selected. Clicking a selected selector again also toggles it off; Ctrl/Cmd-click toggles individual additions.

screenshots.title: Select the columns to remove
screenshots.instruction: Select Qty, then Shift-click UnitPrice. Click Delete selected, or press Delete while the grid selection has focus. A cell text editor keeps normal text-deletion behavior.

screenshots.title: Inspect the reduced design
screenshots.instruction: Only Region and Enabled remain. Click Undo to restore the removed columns and their query settings. A shared expression that still needs a removed operand can block deletion with an explanation.

screenshots.title: Restore the design
screenshots.instruction: Undo restores both columns in one operation. Redo removes them again. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y work while navigating the grid; inside text editors they retain native text undo/redo.

screenshots.title: Select a column and move it earlier
screenshots.instruction: Select UnitPrice, then click Move earlier. Move later moves the selection toward the right. These explicit controls also work on touch screens.

screenshots.title: Check the new order
screenshots.instruction: UnitPrice is now before Qty. You can also drag a desktop column by its dedicated handle. Dragging the resize divider changes width rather than order.

screenshots.title: Widen a column
screenshots.instruction: Drag the slim divider at the right of a column selector. Width stays between 140 and 600 pixels and does not change the query or result-table widths.

screenshots.title: Choose sorting and visibility
screenshots.instruction: In Qty’s Sort cell choose Descending. Uncheck Enabled’s Show checkbox. You can sort by several columns; design order determines their priority when edited.

screenshots.title: Filter by a hidden field
screenshots.instruction: Enter True under Enabled’s Criteria and click Apply query. The result contains 21 enabled source rows, ordered by Qty descending, without displaying Enabled.

screenshots.title: Enter a criterion
screenshots.instruction: Focus the Qty Criteria cell and press Enter/F2. Type > 10, then press Enter to commit it. Clicking once only focuses a cell; Enter/F2 or double-click enters text editing.

screenshots.title: Add an AND condition
screenshots.instruction: On the same Criteria row, enter True under Enabled. This means qty > 10 AND enabled = True.

screenshots.title: Add an OR alternative
screenshots.instruction: Click Add OR row. In Or 1 enter < 5 under Qty and True under Enabled. The query means (qty > 10 AND enabled = True) OR (qty < 5 AND enabled = True). Remove Or 1 deletes that whole alternative.

screenshots.title: Check the expression and result count
screenshots.instruction: Apply query. This example matches 17 of 32 source rows. Expand Readable expression and query clauses to inspect parentheses and the corresponding WHERE clause.

screenshots.title: Open a criterion’s rule editor
screenshots.instruction: Enter "North" under Region. Click the … button in that same Criteria cell. This edits only that cell’s condition; Edit whole expression edits the complete query filter.

screenshots.title: Choose an operator and value
screenshots.instruction: In the rule choose Region, starts with (case-insensitive), and N. The operator choices depend on the field type. Click Apply criterion, or Cancel to keep the old condition. Text comparisons in this Access-style query ignore case.

screenshots.title: Combine the rule with a numeric range
screenshots.instruction: Enter >= 10 And <= 20 under Qty on the same Criteria row, then Apply query. Five North rows match the range. The equivalent Region criterion is Like "N*". Clear criterion in the dialog removes its entire cell condition.

screenshots.title: Open the row-expression editor
screenshots.instruction: With Region = "North" and Qty > 10 on the Criteria row, click Edit row expression in the left gutter. Use + → insert rule to add a condition, or + → insert group for parentheses.

screenshots.title: Add a row-level rule and apply
screenshots.instruction: Choose Enabled, equals, false. Click Apply criterion, then Apply query. The row means region = "North" AND qty > 10 AND enabled = False, which matches 4 source rows. On a separate Or row the row expression belongs to that alternative only.

screenshots.title: Open the whole-expression builder
screenshots.instruction: Start from Reset query and enter True under Enabled. Expand Readable expression and query clauses, then click Edit whole expression. The existing Enabled rule appears inside the root braces. Find the + insertion control after this rule.

screenshots.title: Insert a nested group
screenshots.instruction: Click the + after the Enabled rule to reveal two choices: insert rule and insert group (folder icon). Click Insert group at position 2 to add a parenthesized group beside the existing rule.

screenshots.title: Set AND outside, OR inside
screenshots.instruction: Use the + inside the new parentheses twice to insert two rules. Set the first to Qty / is greater than / 10 and the second to Qty / is less than / 5. Keep AND between Enabled and the group; choose OR between the two Qty rules. This means enabled = True AND (qty > 10 OR qty < 5).

screenshots.title: Apply and inspect the distributed criteria
screenshots.instruction: Click Apply expression in the dialog, then Apply query on the page. The equivalent grid repeats Enabled = True on each OR alternative. The result matches 17 source rows. Cancel in the dialog would discard the complete draft.

screenshots.title: Edit a criterion in Zoom
screenshots.instruction: Focus the Qty Criteria cell and press Shift+F2, or open its cell context menu and choose Zoom. Type > 10 in the larger editor, then click Apply. Cancel or Escape keeps the previous value.

screenshots.title: Clear only the criterion
screenshots.instruction: Right-click the Qty Criteria cell, or focus it and press Shift+F10. Choose Clear Cell to remove its condition while keeping Qty in the design.

screenshots.title: Cancel an invalid draft
screenshots.instruction: Typing > without a value is invalid. The error explains the problem. Correct the draft and press Enter, or press Escape to discard it. Apply query cannot use an unfinished or invalid draft.

screenshots.title: Type an alias and arithmetic expression
screenshots.instruction: Add another Qty occurrence. In its Field text box type LineTotal: [qty]*[price], then Enter. The alias appears as the result heading. Use the source name price, even though its caption is UnitPrice.

screenshots.title: Apply the calculated output
screenshots.instruction: Apply query to calculate LineTotal per source row. You can Show/hide and sort this output. Filter the source fields with Criteria; direct criteria on row-scalar output are disabled. Division by zero is reported as an execution error.

screenshots.title: Add the source wildcard
screenshots.instruction: Click S071_Rows.* in the source card. A wildcard column appears at the right with its own Show control. Existing explicit columns remain, so adding the wildcard can intentionally produce repeated outputs.

screenshots.title: Expand before editing individual fields
screenshots.instruction: Select the wildcard column, then click Expand wildcard (it may be under the toolbar’s More button). This replaces it with separate field occurrences. Direct wildcard sorting is disabled; choose an explicit field instead.

screenshots.title: Use the expanded columns
screenshots.instruction: The wildcard becomes Region, Qty, UnitPrice and Enabled occurrences. Each can now be hidden, sorted, filtered or used with Totals. Existing compatible wildcard criteria are preserved during expansion.

screenshots.title: Enable the Total row
screenshots.instruction: Check Use Totals above the source card. All included columns initially use Group By. Keeping extra Group By fields can create many smaller groups.

screenshots.title: Choose grouping and aggregate functions
screenshots.instruction: Keep Region = Group By. Set Qty = Sum and UnitPrice = Avg. First uncheck Enabled’s Show box, then set its Total operation to Not used so it does not split groups. A shown field must have a Total operation. Numeric-only functions are disabled for nonnumeric fields.

screenshots.title: Read the grouped result
screenshots.instruction: Apply query. There are two result rows: North has SumOfqty 256 and AvgOfprice 3; South has SumOfqty 272 and AvgOfprice 4. The status distinguishes 32 matched source rows from 2 grouped result rows.

screenshots.title: Filter input records with Where
screenshots.instruction: Continue the totals query. Set Enabled’s Total operation to Where, then enter True in its Criteria. Where forces Show off. This filters the input records before Sum and Avg run.

screenshots.title: Filter groups with HAVING
screenshots.instruction: Enter > 170 under the Sum Qty column. Criteria beneath an aggregate or Group By field become HAVING. The condition means Sum(qty) > 170, rather than requiring each source qty to exceed 170.

screenshots.title: Check both stages
screenshots.instruction: Apply query. The enabled filter matches 21 source rows; HAVING leaves only South, with SumOfqty 192. North’s enabled-only sum is 160 and is excluded. Inspect the SQL view for separate WHERE and HAVING clauses.

screenshots.title: Choose Max and Count
screenshots.instruction: Keep Region = Group By. Choose Max for Qty and Count for UnitPrice. Hide Enabled, then choose Not used for it. Count(field) counts non-null field values; Count(*) in a Total Expression counts every input row.

screenshots.title: Read the summary values
screenshots.instruction: Apply query. Each region has 16 non-null price values. North’s maximum Qty is 31; South’s is 32. Min/Max preserve the input type; StDev and Var use sample statistics and need at least two non-null numbers. First/Last follow source-row order within the group, before result sorting.

screenshots.title: Edit an aggregate formula
screenshots.instruction: Keep Region = Group By. For price and enabled first uncheck Show, then choose Not used. In Qty’s Total dropdown choose Expression. Enter Sum([qty]) / Count(*) in the dialog, then click Apply expression.

screenshots.title: Apply and reopen the formula
screenshots.instruction: The grouped output now contains average Qty computed by the formula: North 16 and South 17. Use Edit expression in the Total cell to reopen it. Cancel discards a dialog draft.

screenshots.title: Choose All query clauses
screenshots.instruction: In Expression clause select All query clauses. WHERE and HAVING use condition trees; GROUP BY and ORDER BY use ordered field lists. Scroll within the dialog to reach the lower lists. Apply expression commits all clause drafts together.

screenshots.title: Add an ordered sorting field
screenshots.instruction: Choose ORDER BY — ordered fields in Expression clause to focus just that list. Click Add field, choose [region], then DESC. Entries in this list are evaluated in order. GROUP BY has a similar field list without sort direction. Remove an entry with its Remove control; brace buttons can collapse each list independently.

screenshots.title: Apply all clause changes together
screenshots.instruction: Click Apply expression at the bottom of the dialog, then Apply query. South now precedes North because Region sorts descending. Cancel would discard all clause drafts together.

screenshots.title: Read the generated SQL
screenshots.instruction: Expand SQL view and editor. The current query includes WHERE [qty] > 10. Editing SQL starts a draft; apply or discard that draft before other query changes.

screenshots.title: Apply the SQL draft
screenshots.instruction: Change > 10 to > 20 and click Apply SQL. This updates the visual criteria; click Apply query afterward to update results. Invalid SQL stays in the editor with an error.

screenshots.title: Discard unwanted SQL changes
screenshots.instruction: Discard SQL draft / load current query restores the committed SQL. Here the committed criterion remains > 20. Query results remain at the last successful Apply query.

screenshots.title: Export the current definition
screenshots.instruction: Click Export query JSON, then scroll to Query JSON — export or reload. Copy the text into a file if you want to keep it. The definition includes fields, visibility, sorting, criteria and totals.

screenshots.title: Reload the exported definition
screenshots.instruction: After Reset query, click Reload query JSON to restore and apply the JSON already in the text area. A malformed or incompatible definition reports an error and leaves the previous result visible. Reopen S07.1 for its enhanced definitions.

screenshots.title: Select separate columns on touch
screenshots.instruction: Tap Select columns to enter touch selection mode. Tap Region and UnitPrice selectors to toggle each one independently. Selected 2 confirms the selection. Cancel selection exits this mode.

screenshots.title: Show one full-width column
screenshots.instruction: Tap Focus column, using More if needed. The same grid cells now show one column beside the row labels. This is useful when the virtual keyboard leaves little space.

screenshots.title: Choose another focused field
screenshots.instruction: Use Focused column to switch to Qty, then edit its Criteria. Toggle Focus column again to return to the full grid. Use Apply query below the editor to refresh results.
